issues.legal_issue: A decree enforcing a charge may be passed against property held as an occupancy holding when the statutory prohibition on such a decree has been repealed before the decree is made.
material_facts: The property was held by the appellant as an occupancy tenant.
The trial court declined to enforce the charge against the property, but the High Court granted a decree enforcing it.
The statutory provision containing the prohibition had been repealed before the decree was passed.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was competent to grant a decree enforcing the charge because the prohibition had been repealed before the decree was passed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 12 of the Central Provinces Tenancy Act, 1920 contained the prohibition against passing a decree for sale or foreclosure affecting an occupancy tenant's holding. As that provision had been repealed before the decree was passed, the prohibition did not prevent the decree. No earlier case was cited on this issue.

predicates.occupancy_holding_charge_case: The proceeding concerns enforcement of a charge against property held by the person liable as an occupancy tenant.
predicates.prohibition_repealed_before_decree: The statutory prohibition on granting the relevant decree had been repealed before the decree was made.

issues.definition: When a proceeding concerns a charge against an occupancy holding and the relevant prohibition has been repealed before the decree, a charge decree is permissible.

issues.legal_issue: An appellate court may grant a respondent relief that the trial court omitted even when the respondent did not appeal, if the relief ought in law to have been granted.
material_facts: The trial court declined to enforce the charge against the property.
The respondent did not appeal from that part of the trial court's decree.
The appellant appealed, and the High Court granted the respondent a decree enforcing the charge.
issues.conclusion: The respondent's failure to appeal did not bar the High Court from granting a decree enforcing the charge.
issues.legal_principle: Order 41, Rule 33 of the Code of Civil Procedure empowers an appellate court to pass a decree or order that ought to have been passed and to grant further or other relief as the case requires, including in favour of a respondent who has not appealed. The Court relied on Rodhika Mohan v. Sudhir Chandra and Gum Ram v. Ramji Lal, which explain that the power extends to granting what ought in law to have been granted and what the justice of the case requires.

predicates.appeal_against_decree: A party has brought an appeal challenging a decree made in the proceeding.
predicates.respondent_did_not_appeal: The respondent seeking relief did not file an appeal or objection against the part of the decree that denied that relief.
predicates.omitted_relief_ought_in_law: The appellate court determines that the lower court omitted relief that ought in law to have been granted.

issues.definition: In an appeal against a decree, if the respondent did not appeal but the appellate court determines that the omitted relief ought in law to have been granted, the appellate court may grant that respondent relief.

issues.legal_issue: A challenge asserting that payments were not credited does not succeed when the courts have made concurrent findings on that contention.
material_facts: The appellant contended that payments beyond those acknowledged by the respondent had been made and had not been credited.
The courts had made concurrent findings concerning the payments.
issues.conclusion: The Court rejected the contention that the payments had not all been credited, in view of the concurrent findings of the courts.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on the concurrent findings of the courts below in rejecting the payment contention; it stated no separate statutory provision or earlier case for this issue.

predicates.appeal_against_decree: A party has brought an appeal challenging a decree made in the proceeding.
predicates.concurrent_findings_on_payment_accountin: The courts below made concurrent findings concerning whether the payments at issue had been credited.

issues.definition: In an appeal against a decree, when the courts below have made concurrent findings on payment accounting, the challenge that payments were not credited is rejected.
